summary: Idempotency token re-encoding after HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 downgrade causes duplicated funcall callbacks
description: Customer reports duplicate downstream tool/webhook executions after an intermittent network hiccup. ClearSight observed two identical webhook POSTs for the same funcall within ~10s, despite supplying an idempotency token. The pattern only occurs when requests traverse our edge proxy path that performs HTTP/2 <-> HTTP/1.1 translation (edge-side connection downgrade).
customer_message: We saw duplicate webhook invocations for the same function call when our clients hit the Redwood endpoint through our CDN-backed edge. This started after a bandwidth spike in their region. We consistently send X-Idempotency-Key header and only expect one webhook per funcall. Can you advise why the dedup didn't work?
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Go or Python SDK to initiate a streaming funcall with header X-Idempotency-Key: A1+b/9==token (base64-like with plus and slash)
2) Route traffic through the edge proxy configured to terminate HTTP/2 and proxy to origin over HTTP/1.1 (typical CDN config)
3) Simulate a transient connection reset on the edge (e.g., terminate upstream connection mid-stream) so client retries using SDK exponential backoff
4) Observe downstream webhook receiver logs for duplicated POSTs for the same logical funcall id within rollback window (~30s)
5) Capture raw request headers at edge and origin and compare X-Idempotency-Key values
logs: downstream webhook received (first): id=fn-98321 payload=... ack=200
downstream webhook received (second, ~7s later): id=fn-98321 payload=... ack=200
sdk debug (go): retry attempt=2 replacing connection, idempotency_header_sent=A1+b/9==token
sdk debug (python): retry attempt=1 header_transport=%22A1%2Bb%2F9%3D%3Dtoken%22 (note: URL-encoding observed)
nginx-ingress log: proxy_protocol backend chunked transfer applied; header rewrite enabled: true
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: dedup table keys differ because edge rewrites/percent-encodes special characters (+, /, =) when downgrading HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 or when manipulating header frames.

Confirmed with packet captures: clients send raw token (plus/slash/equals). Edge transforms token to percent-encoded representation when converting header from HTTP/2 pseudo-headers frame to HTTP/1.1 header string in the upstream request.

Go SDK sends header as-is; Python SDK underlying requests library appears to quote/encode header intermittently when connection pooling is torn down mid-stream and a new connection starts over HTTP/1.1 path.
Serving runtime dedup key normalization expects canonical token (raw bytes) and currently treats percent-encoded and raw string as different keys which bypasses dedup check.
Edge configuration has a legacy flag 'encode_non_ascii_headers' set to true for historical infra compatibility; this flag appears to be the culprit for token mutation.
Reproduced locally by toggling edge flag: with encoding flag ON, origin sees percent-encoded token and duplicates observed; flag OFF origin sees raw token and dedup works as expected.
actions_taken: Scoped to dedicated customer's edge path; created INT-3321 to validate edge config change impact across tenants
Temporarily advised customer to URI-safe base64 their idempotency token (replace +/ with -_) as mitigation while we fix server-side normalization
Added logging in serving runtime to decode percent-encoded idempotency tokens to canonical form for dedup-key lookup as short-term protective measure (feature flagged)
Opened runtime PR to canonicalize idempotency header decoding and normalizing both raw and percent-encoded forms (see related PR)
Requested edge team to evaluate disabling header encoding for idempotency header or to preserve original header bytes during HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translations
resolution: Workaround provided and server-side normalization feature-flag enabled for ClearSight. Pending permanent fix: runtime PR merged and scheduled for deployment in next minor (042). Edge config change will be coordinated with infra/edge teams under INT-3321. Marking customer ticket for monitoring; closing after 72h of no duplicates observed.
